speaker: Tara (Village Elder)
transcript_excerpt: When the boys come home from the sea, we greet them with 'aayo-re'. The younger one will never call his elder brother by his first name; he calls him 'toran' or 'toran-ma' if he wants to show true respect.

speaker: Rishi (Fisherman)
transcript_excerpt: Dara-la chora-te? No fresh water today. We have to haul the boat (nau-la) before sunset. If the wind (bayu) gets cold, staying on the water is dangerous.

speaker: Dev (Trade merchant)
transcript_excerpt: In the town market (baza), you meet people from everywhere. Some outsiders use weird words like 'koba' to refer to a rough guy or an estranged elder brother, but our mothers would slap our mouths for using it at home.

speaker: Ananya (Student / Code-switcher)
transcript_excerpt: We code-switch constantly. When we talk with friends, we say 'nira' instead of 'ni-'. Like: 'Koa nira ja-te' instead of 'Koa ni-ja-te'. But with our grandparents, we strictly keep SOV and proper suffixes.

speaker: Kiran (Mountain Guide)
transcript_excerpt: The high bridge (setu) was broken (tutta). We took the secret path (gupt rasta). Sula boro to anyone traveling before dawn.
